Intelligent agents chapter

Intelligent agents: completed chapter audit

Reviewed on 8 October 2026. This chapter is a review draft requiring explicit student approval. The preceding vector-space chapter was approved; no subsequent chapter has started.

Instruction and coverage

The chapter contains 30 sections, including 5,840 words in the lesson before its extended worked bank and end-of-chapter rules. It develops agent boundaries and histories, PEAS, expected-utility rationality, risk and robust decisions, environment classification, reflex and model-based architectures, goals, utility, learning, sufficient state, belief updates, information value, vacuum-world planning, problem formulation, exact abstractions, constrained counting, search nodes and discounted returns. Definitions are accompanied by assumptions, derivations, counterexamples and implementation where useful. Detailed search algorithms, Bayesian-network inference, MDP solution algorithms and reinforcement-learning methods remain explicitly assigned to subsequent chapters.

Four core written courses from four universities were actually read and compared: Berkeley CS188, CMU 15-281, Edinburgh INF2D and Stanford CS221. The source audit records the bounded candidate pool, the exact accessible documents, instructor attribution, shared source provenance, reasons for selection and corrections to introductory simplifications. It does not claim to have surveyed every course worldwide or visually inspected inaccessible third-party pictures.

Worked problems and final rules

There are 80 independently written or attributed reconstructed problems and two authentic MSc examination adaptations, each with a full instructional solution. The bank includes symbolic counts, probability thresholds, conditional expectations, posterior inference, information value, indistinguishable histories, memory requirements, transition models, abstraction failures, state constraints and mathematical counterexamples. Eighty separate concluding rules state their conditions, consequences and failure cases in complete sentences. Relevant questions mount their own applicable subject models rather than a generic animation.

The authentic questions are MSc Computer Engineering 1405, Questions 71 and 75, visually checked against original PDF page 15. Their wording and option order were verified. The answers are independently derived, not attributed to an unverified official key. Question 71 is qualified: the intended environment answer does not mean that sensors and actuators never affect attainable performance. Question 75 preserves the decisive word “only.” No unmatched PhD item is invented or relabelled.

Mathematical review

The finite-action memoryless-policy intersection criterion is stated with its quantifiers and proved in both directions. Bayesian prediction and conditioning are separated; impossible observations never receive invented posteriors. Information-value inequalities require the stated fixed action set and passive sensor assumptions. Vacuum-world counts distinguish physical states from belief supports. Abstractions preserve goal status, legal actions, transition images and costs rather than merely merging similar-looking pictures.

The automated evidence reports 7,470 exact checks. The editable two-state, two-action information laboratory was compared on 601 independently enumerated inputs against a Python Fraction oracle that evaluates all four contingent policies. Tests cover impossible branches, ties, negative utilities, uninformative and perfect sensors, large fractions and invalid inputs. This is evidence for the declared finite models; it is not a proof of all possible implementations or unseen exam performance.

Visual and interactive review

Seventeen specialized models contain 69 authored checkpoints: the agent loop, utility comparisons, probability thresholds, history aliasing, common optimal actions, posterior beliefs, information decision trees, physical vacuum motion, sensorless belief supports, hidden-key transitions, state-versus-node graphs, cyclic paths, discounting, a counter game, PEAS, learning roles and regret. They are mounted at 34 relevant places. Geometry, label padding and bounds were checked for every stored checkpoint. Diagrams use connected arrows and separately styled mathematical labels; the laboratory uses proportionally sized, stacked fractions without stretching short numerators.

The editable laboratory's final checkpoint compares acting without purchase, buying then acting, and the net gain; it displays the actual conditional policy. It no longer repeats the prior action values under a misleading final-value label. Exact numerical labels describe complete checkpoints. Intermediate motion is explicitly described as a geometric transition, not as a newly computed exact solution.

Browser checks passed for fonts, mathematical delimiters and script bases, 17 models / 69 checkpoints, previous/next/reset/seek, genuine in-flight pause and resume, reduced motion, print checkpoints, seven valid laboratory examples, eight invalid inputs preserving the previous valid result, a 390-pixel mobile viewport, chapter-library navigation and the Week 3 link. No runtime errors or underlined text were found. Representative information-tree, vacuum and final laboratory screenshots were manually inspected after the final revision.

Typography and retention

English prose uses Source Sans 3, headings use Newsreader, mathematics uses STIX Two Math and code uses JetBrains Mono. Native MathML represents mathematical formulas, including grouped script bases and complete fences. The chapter's checked HTML contains 664 mathematical instances; the browser includes additional generated laboratory mathematics. Desktop diagrams fit their panel; small screens retain intentional internal diagram scrolling.

All 43 preceding chapter HTML files retain their recorded SHA-256 hashes. Their 2,757 worked questions remain present. The resulting library has 44 chapters and 2,839 questions. The new chapter remains a draft until approval.

Remaining limits

Public-source availability bounds the candidate comparison. The examination evidence is limited to the original pages explicitly checked, with no unverified official answer key claimed. The audits support the stated scope and tested models; literal universal coverage, zero future errors and guaranteed performance on every unseen question cannot be certified. Publication status is recorded separately and must be checked before describing the online Site as updated.
